title: Comic
description: Comic, in comic book cinematography, inks a live-action frame: hard edges, halftone in the shadows, limited spots of color, a page that still has a photographed body in it. The camera still has a lens and one sun, and it is not a screenshot of a book.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Origin stories, punchlines, a city that should look published: the person still occupies space, but print law sits on top of the photograph. One lighting direction so the ink has a sun.
No speech balloons. Models ruin letters.
Dialogue can survive if the ink is gentle and the faces stay human. It is the wrong tool when you need documentary pores and no line, or when you actually wanted full Animation.
If there is no grain or halation of a camera, you left live action and drew a still.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Lock a 35mm or 50mm at eye height. One hard or hard-soft key so edges have a side.
Ask for inked contours, halftone in shadows, a face that is still a photograph. Limited color spots.
No balloons. Prompt: Comic-book treatment of [Subject], inked edges, halftone, panel energy, a page that moves.
For video, the print holds while the body makes one small action.

blocks.text: A punchline, an origin beat, a city that should look printed. Do not use it as a cartoon filter on a whispering drama, and do not add balloons.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Dick Tracy uses spot color and hard makeup as print law on photographed faces. Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse is animation you may borrow as a grade language, not as a frame to copy.
The still should look printable.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: Over-processing into a cartoon with no lens, or stacking this with Ink Riot and oil. The tell is no camera grain and no sun.
Fix it: one light direction, halftone in shadows, face still a photograph.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Comic in film?
Live-action coverage wearing print law: inked edges, halftone, limited color, a photographed body. The camera still has a lens. It is not a scan of a comic page.
Comic vs Animation
Animation is drawn as the whole image. Comic keeps photographic structure and adds ink and halftone. If there is no lens, you left this look.
When should I use Comic?
Origin beats, punchlines, a published city. Skip it when you need plain documentary skin, and skip balloons.
How do I prompt Comic for AI image or video?
Name subject, lens, and one key, then: Comic-book treatment of [Subject], inked edges, halftone, panel energy, a page that moves. Forbid speech balloons. Keep the face photographic.
